source_name: ROK Ministry of Unification - North Korea Information Portal (정보통신/ICT industry overview, updated 2023.7)
note: 해주반도체공장 (Haeju Semiconductor Factory) listed among DPRK semiconductor plants (alongside Pyongyang IC plant, Tanchon plant) in ROK government compilation. Computing-hardware manufacturing facility, NOT a data center. No data-center evidence found in South Hwanghae.
No real data center / IT center facility evidence for South Hwanghae (capital: Haeju). Only semiconductor-manufacturing lead above; external verifiability essentially nil.

source_name: NK Economy (relaying DPRK state media Arirang Meare)
note: Video forest-fire surveillance system completed in North Hwanghae by forestry officials together with provincial electronic-affairs research institute (전자업무연구소) technicians; 20 camera monitoring sites across cities/counties. Application-level IT deployment, NOT a data center.
No data center / IT center facility evidence found in North Hwanghae (capital: Sariwon). Only app-level IT deployments (wildfire monitoring); treat as U.

Two people in Wonsan (Kangwon capital) arrested for 'smishing' scam using malware-laden text messages to steal from donju; indicates local IT/cyber-capable actors in Wonsan. No facility-level evidence.

No data center / IT center facility evidence for Kangwon (capital: Wonsan). Wonsan universities (Jong Jun-thaek Univ. of Economics, Wonsan Agricultural Univ., Wonsan Fisheries Univ.) are not IT-focused; treat as U.

source_name: ROK Ministry of Unification - North Korea Information Portal (정보통신, IT industry overview)
note: 함흥컴퓨터기술대학 (Hamhung Computer Technology University) established 2001 as one of the DPRK's two computer-technology universities (with Pyongyang); together with Pyongsong Science Univ. and ~10 central universities it graduates 5,000-10,000 IT workers/year. Real IT-education/computing institution in Hamhung, South Hamgyong (corroborated by multiple sources).

source_name: NK News (Dagyum Ji, citing Rodong Sinmun)
note: Rodong Sinmun: 37 universities nationwide opened 85 new departments specializing in information security, robotics, nano-engineering; Hamhung University of Pharmacology opened a medical-equipment department. National IT-education expansion applies to provincial universities including South Hamgyong.

A Hamhung student was caught using illicit software to access foreign data as DPRK cracks down on banned-information distribution; indicates grassroots IT/cyber activity in Hamhung. Not a facility; C/U.

Profile of 함흥컴퓨터기술대학 (Hamhung Computer Technology University): founded 1985 as 함흥전자계산기단과대학; trains advanced computer/applied-computer engineers for the information-telecom sector. Personal blog, low authority; C.

source_name: NK Economy (relaying DPRK state media Chosun Today)
note: 함경북도전자업무연구소 (North Hamgyong Province Electronic Affairs Research Institute) newly built in Chongjin per Chosun Today: program-development office and R&D offices; aims at informatization of production/management across the province incl. an intranet data-access system (국가자료통신망); Kim Jong-un reviewed construction plans. Real provincial IT facility (state-media claim, externally unverifiable).
Reported surge of youth in Chongjin and other major cities seeking computer/IT (정보통신) skills training; indicates growing IT training/demand ecosystem in North Hamgyong, not a facility per se.

혜산청년광산 (Hyesan Youth Mine) in Ryanggang implemented computer control systems across its production process (camera monitoring, computer logging of dressing/mining/power/drainage systems). Computing deployment in mining, NOT a data center.
No data center / IT center evidence found in Ryanggang (capital: Hyesan). Only the mine-automation lead above; treat as U.

KT announced building a ~3,000-pyong (~9,900 m²) communications center inside the Kaesong Industrial Complex by 2007 for wired/wireless voice and internet service for tenant firms; KT also negotiating with the DPRK side for additional telecom-equipment imports. Real telecom/data-communications facility at Kaesong (complex closed since Feb 2016).

Satellite analysis of the KIC (closed 2016): renewed activity since 2021-2023 incl. the electronics/electricity sector and the Jaeyoung Solutech Telecom Components building in mixed industries; complex being refurbished/repurposed by DPRK. Telecom/electronics facility evidence at Kaesong, not a dedicated data center.

source_name: UN Security Council Resolution 2270 (2016) - official UN text
note: UNSCR 2270 strengthened sanctions against the DPRK: ROK closed the Kaesong Industrial Complex in Feb 2016; the resolution required member states to close joint ventures/cooperative entities with DPRK entities and freeze DPRK-designated assets - official sanctions documentation framing Kaesong-area industrial facilities.

ROK Ministry of Unification announced temporary closure of the Kaesong Industrial Complex in response to DPRK nuclear test and satellite launch; end of KIC operations including its communications/data infrastructure.
